newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end lower as bullion dips.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end lower as bullion dips.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures extended early losses to end sharply lower on Wednesday, depressed by a slip in bullion prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 15 yen to 20 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off 1,376 yen.
"Although private investors hunted for bargains for most of the day, selling pressure from overseas investors in the spot gold market put a downward pressure on gold futures," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $341.25/65 per ounce at 0719 GMT, against $341.70/342.20 in New York on Tuesday.

Bargain-hunting buying in gold futures was countered by trade houses' selling, while trade houses bought spot gold in arbitrage dealings. "Spot gold edged down as overseas selling absorbed Japanese buying, which suggested overseas investors were building fresh longs in anticipation of a further dip," the trader said.
The traders said they pegged the initial support at around $338.50 per ounce, and a break below the level could batter gold further with no bullish factors in sight.
Palladium futures settled sharply lower as selling gathered force in the afternoon, with Russian spot sales looming.
A perception that the yen's dip has now stalled, also dampened sentiment.

Traders said there were rumours that the central bank in Russia is likely to take charge of platinum group exports from PGM export agency Almaz, and traders were divided over the possible impact if that happens.

Palladium futures ranged from nine yen to 21 yen per gram lower, with benchmark February ending down nine yen at 586 yen. Benchmark February platinum was off six yen per gram at 1,455 yen. Benchmark February silver was off 0.6 yen per 10 grams at 192.4 yen.
